text:
matt: ran an nsys capture on dedicated-prod-3 during the regen workload. seeing a tight hotspot in the decode path, not the matmul we expected. posting the quick top-kernel summary from the trace.

matt: top kernels by total GPU time (nsys summary):
- fused_attn_qkv_fwd      38.2%  1.12s
- kv_cache_read          19.5%  0.57s
- softmax_forward         6.7%  0.20s
- gelu_fwd                5.1%  0.15s
- decode_dispatch         4.8%  0.14s
- small_matmul_launches   4.2%  0.12s
- layernorm_fwd           3.9%  0.11s
- launch_overhead         3.5%  0.10s
(remaining kernels <3% each)

matt: timeline shows ~800 repeated short kernel launches for kv_cache_read + small_matmul_launches across the seq dimension. SM util peaked but avg SM utilization is ~36%, memory bw low (~22% of peak). suggests launch/serialization overhead + non-coalesced KV loads.

priya: can you paste the nsys command and the short timeline snippet? also which model size?

matt: model = 13B, decode length 64, beam=1. nsys cmd I ran:

```
nsys profile --output=/tmp/trace_dedicated3 --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --duration=60 --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi
```

matt: here is the perf table excerpt from the capture (copied):

```
Kernel Name              Calls  Total Time (ms)  Avg (ms)  % GPU Time
fused_attn_qkv_fwd       120    1120.3           9.34      38.2
kv_cache_read            760     569.8           0.75      19.5
softmax_forward         240     199.6           0.83       6.7
gelu_fwd               180     152.1           0.85       5.1
small_matmul_launches  820     123.9           0.15       4.2
```

julia: 2 quick thoughts: 1) kv_cache_read has lots of tiny calls -> check coalescing and whether we can switch to a strided batched read (fewer launches). 2) small_matmul_launches + launch_overhead -> our batching heuristic might be creating too many single-token matmuls instead of grouping requests.

julia: SM occupancy numbers from the capture?

matt: occupancy snapshot from the run: average active warps/SM = 0.48, achieved occupancy ~48%, achieved sm_efficiency ~36%. L2 utilization low, global mem throughput ~22% of peak.

carlos: this smells like the KV read kernel isn't using vectorized loads. can you check the kernel source for `kv_cache_read` in the fused runtime (commit d4f7b2) — last change added per-sample offsets. might have regressed coalescing.

matt: good call, that commit changed index math. i'll diff.

priya: other lever: increase continuous-batching window from 8ms -> 15ms to accumulate more tokens into one matmul batch. That trades tail latency vs throughput but should reduce small launches. Also consider merging softmax + scaling into the attn kernel to remove separate softmax_forward calls.

julia: agree. also try compiling the fused_attn kernel with smaller block size to increase occupancy for the specific sequence length distribution: test blockDim.x = 128 -> 256 and compare sm_efficiency.

matt: quick nvprof check on dev box (short run) shows that when we increase batch grouping to 2x, kv_cache_read calls drop by ~60% and small_matmul_launches drop by ~55% and total GPU time for decode path goes down ~28%.

nsys-bot: automated-metrics: triggered perf regression check for commit d4f7b2. baseline: 1769982340, head: d4f7b2 -> regression detected in decode tail latency (+18%).

carlos: let's bisect that commit range tomorrow. for immediate mitigations: revert the per-sample offsets change (or add a coalescing path), bump batching window, and add a fused softmax option.

matt: i'll send a small patch to add a coalesced read path and a feature flag to enable fused-softmax at runtime. i'll also schedule an nsys capture with perf metrics focused on L2 and memory throughput next run.

priya: thanks — please post the new nsys trace here once done. if patch helps, we can ship as a fastfix for dedicated clusters.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for fix branch matt/kv-coalesced at 1778001400 to dedicated-prod-3. monitor: infra.metrics/redwood/decode-latency.

matt: noted, will follow the canary and post nsight link when available. :thumbsup:
